2.8.m: Long ago, indeed, a wise sage named Raibhya, whose wealth was austerity,

Then, dispatched by him, she, walking with the grace of an elephant, went;

Adorned with white pearls against the gold of her bodily luster,

With the wavy white brilliance of the corner of her oblique eyes,
she made her lower lip resemble the hue of a fresh sprout. (93)
With a mango blossom hanging by her ear, rich in humming bees,
she was like a Pārijāta creeper arisen from the interior of nectar. (94)
Slender-waisted, broad-hipped, her breasts blooming in beauty,

Once, that protector of subjects, having entrusted the earth to his ministers,

Due to sins arising from a previous birth that indicated misfortune,

Once, while wandering alone in the forest engaged in hunting,

2.8.m: 2. Brahmā's arrival at Ayodhyā; the performance of a sacrifice having undertaken the pilgrimage and other rites; the establishment of Brahmakuṇḍa in his own name; the description of the māhātmya of Brahmakuṇḍa by Lord Brahmā; the māhātmya of the Ṛṇamocanatīrtha situated on the bank of the Sarayū; the description of the māhātmya of the Pāpamocanatīrtha by Lomaśa; the description of the māhātmya of Sahasradhārā by Agastya. 276 1

2.8.s: 4 dharmaharimāhātmyam, tatra dharmarājakṛtanartanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavata āgamanam, dharmeṇa bhagavatstutikaraṇam, bhagavatā dharmarājāya varapradānam, raghusaṃjñakena rājñā digvijayaṃ kṛtvā sūryājñayā kṛtasya sarvasvadakṣiṇanāmakasya yajñasya parisamāpteranaṃtaraṃ kautsaṛṣerāgamanam, svapūjanārthamānītaṃ saṃbhāraṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitena kautsarṣiṇā dhanābhāvāddātraṃtaraṃ prati gantuṃ svecchāprakaṭanam, kautsāya dravyaṃ dātuṃ kauberīṃ saṃpattimādātuṃ kuberajigīṣayā raghoḥ prasthānam, raghubhiyā kubereṇa dravyavṛṣṭikaraṇam, kautsāya raghuṇā sarvadravyadānavarṇanam, kautsena raghurājāyāśīrvādadānavarṇanam, kautsasya svāśramagamanam, svarṇakhanimāhātmyavarṇanam ... 279 2

2.8.m: 4. The māhātmya of Dharmahari; there, the arrival of the Lord upon seeing the dance performed by Dharmarāja; the Lord's praise by Dharma; the Lord's granting of a boon to Dharmarāja; after the completion of the sacrifice named Sarvasvadakṣiṇā performed by the command of Sūrya by the king named Raghu having conquered all directions, the arrival of the seer Kautsa; the expression of his desire to go to another donor due to lack of wealth by the seer Kautsa astonished at seeing the provisions brought for his own worship; Raghu's departure with the desire to conquer Kubera in order to obtain the wealth of Kubera to give wealth to Kautsa; Kubera's shower of wealth out of fear of Raghu; the description of the donation of all the wealth by Raghu to Kautsa; the bestowing of a blessing upon King Raghu by Kautsa; Kautsa's departure to his own hermitage; the description of the māhātmya of Svarṇakhani. 279 2
